items.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well, there was a Cuban, a friend of his, a gentleman called Carrito, who used to pick up grass for him...

ctx.x: Yes, exactly on that date. Do you know anything about that? I know there are a lot of rumors, a lot of stories...

Well, there was a Cuban, a friend of his, a gentleman called Carrito, who used to pick up grass for him... It was very difficult at that time. If it’s still hard, imagine, you know, THEN. And he didn’t like what he brought, whatever, and he smacked him, open-handed in a bar. That gentleman was a marksman in the army. He went home... All his friends were, “Hey, are you going to let him do that to you?” He came back and blew him away.
Well, let’s go back to talking about Mario Bauzá.
